correctness.rationale: The necessary direction applies the source confluences to every lower-to-upper intuitionistic comparison, forcing A-to-B targets to the modal greatest class on B and B-to-A targets to the greatest class on A. Modal transitivity makes the sources predecessor-closed, saturates each top class and forces no extra edges. The converse checks each possible mixed composition and both confluences on all cross-level comparisons, establishing an exact unique bijection. Four disjoint cases by existence of the two top classes give the counting identity for every finite \(p,q\ge2\). The standalone script exhaustively compared literal quantified-frame tests against the full constructed relation sets for all eight shapes of up to five total worlds, with no mismatches (4,20,20,89,189,189,762,762), and verified aggregate preorder statistics through five worlds and larger counts by the exact formula. Finite experiments corroborate, but do not replace, the unbounded-in-size proof.

value.rationale: The complete height-two antichain order with \(p,q\ge2\) is a canonical full two-parameter family, not a hand-picked list of small examples. It is the minimal natural order family allowing branching in both the source and target levels, where existing total-chain endpoint arguments fail and source-specific modal greatest classes interact across both directions. The classification is constructive and complete, and reduces finite modal relation generation from unconstrained binary matrices to within-level preorders and independently chosen downsets. It supplies exact, nontrivial natural frame counts and a reusable finite S4I test family (\(N_{2,2}=89\), \(N_{2,3}=762\), \(N_{3,3}=5922\)). It does not require a general logical theorem or algorithmic complexity breakthrough to be mathematically meaningful.
